lessons.prepare: Open the consolidation chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

slides.title: Unit 1 retrieval and practice priorities
body: Unit 1 · Week 15 · Lesson 1
Identify a specific skill to practise using evidence.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Identify a specific skill to practise using evidence. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: Trace one comparison and one loop update.
Explain a local versus remote destination.
slides.notes: Use brief mixed prompts. Ask for reasoning before showing answers. The purpose is to choose practice, not rank students. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Consolidation stations
slides.notes: Use the existing consolidation chapter. Choose stations from actual errors rather than attempting every activity superficially. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A useful priority
body: Broad label: I am bad at arrays.
Specific priority: I confuse index and value.
Practice: trace a first maximum with a tie.
slides.notes: Model a small, observable learning need. An explanation with a correct changed example provides better evidence than a broad self-label. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A short mixed check
body: Try an index question and a boundary question.
Explain your reasoning with a partner.
Compare with the chapter’s explanations.
slides.notes: Use [8,3,6] index 1 equals 3, and total >= 50 includes 50. Ask students to explain why, then change the values. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Choose two evidence-based practice priorities.
Select matching chapter stations.
Write an expected outcome for each activity.
slides.notes: Support students to separate knowledge gaps, tracing errors and unclear explanations. Keep goals small enough for the remaining lessons. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: A test answer is wrong.
A: Practise every topic for the same time.
B: Identify the mistaken step and choose matching practice.
slides.notes: B. Targeted practice responds to the evidence while mixed retrieval still checks other areas. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Name one priority and the evidence for it.
State the activity you will try next.
slides.notes: A useful plan connects the particular error, the practice task and an observable corrected result. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Programming traces and repairs
body: Unit 1 · Week 15 · Lesson 2
Trace pseudocode and verify a targeted correction.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Trace pseudocode and verify a targeted correction. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: Where does an accumulator start?
How does a first-maximum tie rule work?
slides.notes: A running sum normally starts at zero before the loop. For first maximum, start from a real element after an empty check and update only for a greater value. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Trace a first maximum
slides.notes: Use a strict greater-than comparison. Equality keeps the earlier index. The total is 10, a separate calculation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A reset inside the loop
body: Predict the output for [2, 0, 5].
Find the first loss of an earlier contribution.
slides.code:
for value in [2, 0, 5]:
    total = 0
    total += value
print(total)
slides.notes: The faulty result is 5 because total is reset each pass. Move initialisation before the loop and retest to obtain 7. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Pseudocode transfer
body: Trace load, display and total algorithms.
Translate the loop endpoints into Python range.
Check zero-based indices and stop exclusion.
slides.notes: Use station B’s supplied pseudocode. Do not silently assume all pseudocode conventions use identical endpoint rules. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Repair one faulty traversal from station C.
Test empty, one-item, repeated and negative data.
Explain the cause and the retest results.
slides.notes: Keep the failed trace and changed example. A correct maximum on positive data alone will not expose an initial-zero bug. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: A maximum search starts with value 0 on [-8, -3].
A: It can report a value absent from the list.
B: Zero is always a safe largest-value baseline.
slides.notes: A. The correct maximum is -3. An index initialised to zero is a different idea from a maximum value initialised to zero. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Explain one loop-boundary or initialisation correction.
Give a new input that would expose the old fault.
slides.notes: Require a causal explanation and discriminating test, not merely a rewritten line. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Files, source use and network practice
body: Unit 1 · Week 15 · Lesson 3
Connect operational requirements to useful evidence.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Connect operational requirements to useful evidence. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: What happens when a file opens in w mode?
Does public source visibility grant reuse rights?
slides.notes: Write mode truncates existing contents. Visible source alone does not grant a licence. Use the current textbook licence guidance and recorded permissions. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Requirement and evidence
table: Invalid text followed by valid input
slides.notes: These are independent evidence checks. A screenshot that a screen opened cannot establish all of them. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: The second-run failure
body: First run saves quantity 2.
Second run saves quantity 5.
Only 5 remains. Explain the likely code path to inspect.
slides.notes: Inspect truncating mode and when the file is opened. Correct in a disposable copy and verify two separate records persist. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A library explanation
body: State one access requirement.
Match a control and a positive/negative test.
Identify a useful network diagram correction.
slides.notes: Use station E and the existing support booklet. Keep the traffic policy and application/file permissions distinct. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Complete one station D and one station E activity.
Record expected and actual or justified paper results.
Explain one source or evidence limitation.
slides.notes: Provide the project workbook and course symbol reference. Written network reasoning does not replace the required drawing practice. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: A tutorial is credited but its reuse terms are unclear.
A: Credit alone settles redistribution permission.
B: Check the licence or permission conditions.
slides.notes: B. Attribution and permission answer different questions. Avoid inventing a blanket rule about every copyright exception. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Show one corrected file or network explanation.
State one remaining check before you trust it.
slides.notes: Look for a precise test or source check connected to the claimed result. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

lessons.title: Fresh transfer and a revision plan
lessons.prepare: Open the consolidation chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

slides.title: Fresh transfer and a revision plan
body: Unit 1 · Week 15 · Lesson 4
Apply a corrected idea using changed data.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Apply a corrected idea using changed data. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: What was your priority at the start of this week?
Which independent result now supports improvement?
slides.notes: Return to the selected error, correction and changed example. Do not use a copied answer as the only evidence. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A small revision plan
slides.notes: The dates and priorities belong to the learner. Spaced retry supports checking whether understanding lasts. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A changed minimum example
body: Predict the first minimum’s value and index.
Explain the comparison rule.
slides.notes: The first minimum is -7 at index 2 using a strict less-than update. An empty list needs a separate no-minimum rule. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A changed network case
body: Destination: 192.168.41.10.
Explain the network comparison and next device role.
slides.notes: Networks .40.0 and .41.0 differ under /24, so ordinary off-subnet traffic uses the local gateway/router. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Try one fresh programming and one network problem.
Check with the explained answers afterwards.
Plan a later independent retry for one weak point.
slides.notes: Use changed context or values. Students keep their corrections; this is not a new graded task. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: A changed example still produces the same mistake.
A: Copy the answer and stop.
B: Revisit the decision rule and try another example.
slides.notes: B. Diagnose the repeated error before adding more undirected practice. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Write a priority, practice method and later retry.
Name the result that would show a correction.
slides.notes: A clear plan identifies a skill and an observable outcome rather than a general promise to study more. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.
